title: Evaluation of the project "Digital networking in conservative ophthalmology" (DIVA)
summary:
Diabetes can lead to diseases of the retina, a part of the back of the eye. People with diabetes are therefore advised to have this part of their eyes examined regularly. Capacity for these examinations in ophthalmology practices is limited, which likely results in people not taking advantage of them often enough. “Digital Networking in Conservative Ophthalmology” (DIVA) is a new form of care in Thuringia that allows people with diabetes to have their retinas examined without having to visit an ophthalmologist. Instead, as part of this new care model, a fully automated photograph of the retina is taken, which is then evaluated by an ophthalmologist at a later date.
The study described here uses scientific methods to assess how successful the introduction of this new examination method has been (e.g., whether the number of examinations could be increased) and which factors may have contributed to its success.
